label: Kaggle
terms_note: Kaggle's public API (the one the official `kaggle` CLI and kagglesdk use). The CLI docs document the operations; the HTTP shape (POST https://api.kaggle.com/v1/<service>/<method> with a JSON body) comes from the official kagglesdk package source (v0.1.28). Competition rules must be accepted on kaggle.com before data download or submission.

fields.name: api_token
fields.help: Kaggle API token from https://www.kaggle.com/settings/api ('Generate New Token'; the value the CLI reads from KAGGLE_API_TOKEN / ~/.kaggle/access_token). Sent as Authorization: Bearer.

adapter.rate_note: No rate limit published for the public API. One request per second.

discover.note: `kaggle competitions list` (ListCompetitions {search, page}); `id` is the competition ref (URL suffix, e.g. `titanic`) that the other tools take. The page size is the server default (20; `limit` is not sent) and the response has no total. `kind` and `status` are not sent (the CLI's group/category enums do not match the vocabulary). tags (objects), teamCount, userHasEntered and userRank stay in `raw`.

get_competition.note: GetCompetition {competitionName: <ref>}. `submission_format` is the evaluation metric name; maxDailySubmissions, maxTeamSize, mergerDeadline and isKernelsSubmissionsOnly (code competition) stay in `raw`.

standings.note: `kaggle competitions leaderboard -s` (GetLeaderboard, public leaderboard in rank order). Only the first page: the API pages with nextPageToken, which the vocabulary's `page` cannot carry. `score` is a string in the API, so it stays in `raw.score` (with teamId); there is no rank field, rows come in leaderboard order.

my_entries.note: `kaggle competitions submissions <COMPETITION>` (ListSubmissions): your submissions for one competition, so `competition_id` is required in practice. publicScore/privateScore are strings in the API and stay in `raw`, with description, fileName and errorDescription.

not_offered.me: No account or whoami operation in the CLI docs or CompetitionApiService.
not_offered.enter: No join operation: competition rules are accepted on the competition page at kaggle.com (the CLI docs have no join/accept command).
not_offered.submit: CLI docs: `kaggle competitions submit <COMPETITION> -f <FILE_NAME> -m <MESSAGE>` — a file upload (StartSubmissionUpload, blob upload, then CreateSubmission); binary uploads are out of scope.

evidence: host api.kaggle.com: DNS ok, TLSv1.3 (Google Trust Services)
probe: 4/4 tools answered on their documented path with an auth refusal, a validation error or data; control route -> 404 (not_found), so the answers are path-specific

HTML docs spot-check (render-doc): 0/4 tool paths found verbatim on their docs pages; names not found on the page: get_competition:competitionName, my_entries:competitionName, standings:competitionName, standings:pageSize
